chapters.title: The real CubXL, Ben's idea and his measurements
The same machine as a model
The doser's parts, one at a time

run_captions.caption: 1  Home: GRBL drives the gantry to +Y, the back. The steel tab on its right side plate stops against the docked shuttle
2  Magnets on: two 5 V, 0.3 A electromagnets, switched by the doser's own board. A dock switch and a Hall sensor tell CubOS the doser is home and coupled
3  Forward to vial 1, outlet up at −10°: moving forwards, the tab pulls the shuttle through the magnets
4  Tilt to 35°: the tip drops 36 mm, to 17 mm over the rim, 129 mm behind the capper
5  Dose 20 mg: the vibration motor runs and the auger turns about 0.05 turn (estimates: 380 mg per turn, 10 mg/s)
6  Back to park, −10°: the capillary slopes back into the tube, so shaking while towed should move powder back, not out
7  Back to vial 2: moving back, the tab pushes the shuttle by contact. Then the same cycle, 50 mg
8  Vials 3 and 4: 100 and 200 mg. The dose series doubles; the front four vials are also in the capper's and the pipette's reach
9  Vial 6, at the back of the row: only the doser reaches the back four vials. 50 mg
10  The head works in front of the doser: it runs to its right end and back. No part of the doser is ever in front of the beam's front face
11  Back to the dock: the tab pushes the shuttle home
12  Magnets off: the doser stays on its dock, on its rail. With the power cut, it stays where it is
13  The gantry goes on without it. The four front vials can now be capped or pipetted by the head
